name: Brazzaville
subtitle: Brazzaville, capital of Congo: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 2,145,783 people live in Brazzaville (preliminary results of the 2023 census) (counted 2023).
Brazzaville has 2,145,783 inhabitants, or 34.9 percent of the Congolese population, according to the preliminary 2023 census results.
The department of Brazzaville has a population density of 3,646.81 inhabitants per km2, far denser than most other departments.

parts.text: Brazzaville has 2,145,783 inhabitants, or 34.9 percent of the Congolese population, according to the preliminary 2023 census results.
The department of Brazzaville has a population density of 3,646.81 inhabitants per km2, far denser than most other departments.
Brazzaville lies on the right bank of the Congo River, in the south-east of the country.
France's presence on the right bank of the Congo goes back to 1880, and Brazzaville was born in 1884, named after Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza.

As a colonial capital, Brazzaville was built at a break-of-bulk point of the indigenous trade, 500 km from the Atlantic, combining commercial, administrative, military, religious and residential functions.
In 1940 Brazzaville became the capital of Free France, and in 1944 it hosted the French African Conference.
After the war Brazzaville developed into a modern capital, with a growing airport and many new buildings, though its urban plan remained unfinished.
Brazzaville is administratively divided into districts including Makélékélé, Bacongo, Poto-Poto, Moungali, Ouenzé, Talangaï, Mfilou, Madibou and Djiri, plus the Île Mbamou district.
Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire together house 58.1 percent of the Congolese population.

parts.text: 2,145,783 in 2023, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Brazzaville (the department/commune of Brazzaville, 588 km2), preliminary results of the fifth general census (RGPH-5) of 17 May 2023, presented 29 December 2023.

items.text: Brazza obtained, through a treaty with King Makoko Iloo I, France's possession of the Congo.
Brazzaville was born, named after Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza.
Brazzaville became the capital of Free France.
Brazzaville hosted the French African Conference.
The Basilique Sainte-Anne, begun in 1943, was inaugurated although the works were not yet finished.
The Poto-Poto 'Atelier d'art africain', begun in 1946, was made official as the 'Centre d'art africain'.
On 3 October the mausoleum holding the remains of Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza and his family was inaugurated.
President Sassou Nguesso inaugurated on 18 February the first module of the rebuilt Marché Total.
The preliminary RGPH-5 census counted 2,145,783 people in Brazzaville.

blocks.q: Myth or fact: The Poto-Poto School of Painting is a school located in the Poto-Poto district.
blocks.explain: A Dépêches de Brazzaville feature notes that it is not located in Poto-Poto but in Moungali, and that it is more an art workshop than a school, created in 1951 by Pierre Lods.
